tool_input.description: Confirm tests fail on the seeded regression

result:
`bun run typecheck` and `bun test` both pass (6 tests, 0 failures, green across repeated runs).

The root cause was in `app/Http/Controllers/ProfileController.ts`: `update()` was reading the request body raw with `this.request.json<ProfileInput>()` and then spreading it into `User.forceUpdate()`, so nothing was validated and mass-assignment protection was bypassed — any key in the JSON body (`id`, `passwordHash`, …) was written straight to the account row. The project already had `ProfileUpdateSchema` in `app/Http/Validators/ProfileValidator.ts` encoding exactly the rules the report asks for (trimmed name, required, ≤120 chars; required, lowercased, well-formed email; optional password of at least 8 characters with `''` meaning "keep current"), so the fix was to route the body through `this.validateBody(ProfileUpdateSchema)` — which raises a 422 `ValidationException` with per-field messages the profile page already renders, before the duplicate-email check or any write happens — and to destructure only `name`, `email`, and `password` into `User.update()` instead of `forceUpdate()`, so unknown keys are dropped by the schema and the model's `fillable`/hidden-column rules apply on the way in. I also added `tests/ProfileController.test.ts`, a feature test that signs a real user in over HTTP with a CSRF token and covers the four reported cases: bad email and empty name are rejected with 422 and leave the row untouched, a short password is rejected, and a valid update with extra `id`/`passwordHash` fields succeeds while saving only the name and lowercased email.
